purpose: R1 canary files have a conflict-free ownership proposal — an R0 exit criterion. This is a PROPOSAL for the next round, not authorization to write it.
law: R1 is not open. No lane below may write until Codex audits R0 and the owner opens R1.

correctionNotice.whatWasWrong: the previous version asserted `ownershipCollisions: []` and `conflictFree: true` as literals while four concrete parent/child overlaps existed. A boolean written into a receipt is not proof; nothing computed it and nothing could have failed.
correctionNotice.rootCause: each writeSet was built by taking the family's `sourceOwner` from family-inventory.json and appending `/**`. `sourceOwner` is a RESOLUTION POINTER — where the family resolves from — not a WRITE BOUNDARY. For three families the pointer is the whole category directory (pattern/data/pattern-data-table -> patterns/data, structure/shell/app-shell -> structures/shell, pattern/shell/pattern-page-shell -> patterns/shell), so `patterns/data/**` swallowed four sibling families owned by three other lanes.
correctionNotice.whyTheGateMissedIt: validateConflictGraph compared write sets with exact string equality (`writerByFile.has(file)`), so `patterns/data/**` and `patterns/data/list-toolbar/**` were simply two different strings. Containment was structurally invisible, so no broad parent could ever turn the check red.
whatChanged: write sets rebuilt from the real tree; PatternDataTable narrowed from the whole patterns/data category to patterns/data/data-table
CollectionHeader-PageShell narrowed from patterns/shell to patterns/shell/page-shell, leaving cockpit-header, workbench-header and feature-workspace-frame unclaimed rather than silently swallowed
the AppShell within-lane redundancy (structures/shell/** listed alongside its own child structures/shell/bottom-tab-bar/**) removed
two singleton integrator lanes added so barrels, shared contracts and tests have a declared owner instead of leaking into family globs
the conflict-free claim replaced by a computed verdict produced by executable tooling

ownershipModel.ruling: sourceOwner resolves a family; a writeSet bounds a writer. They are different questions and must not be derived from one another by string concatenation.
ownershipModel.familyWriterBoundary: the family's own folder, minus everything the orchestration contract reserves for a singleton integrator.
ownershipModel.integratorBoundary: category barrels and manifests plus shared contracts belong to the architecture-integrator; tests, drills, i18n parity and evidence belong to the quality-integrator. Both are singleton lane classes in agent-orchestration.json.
ownershipModel.sharedFileRule: if two lanes would need the same file, that file moves to a singleton integrator and the family-writers declare a request. Two writers on one file is never the resolution.
ownershipModel.unclaimedSiblingsAreDeliberate: patterns/shell/{cockpit-header,workbench-header,feature-workspace-frame} and the fifteen non-canary patterns/data families are outside every writeSet. R1 canaries are a calibration subset, not a migration of the whole category; an unclaimed sibling is correct and a swallowed one is not.

notVacuous.claim: a write set pointing at a path that does not exist expands to nothing and would look conflict-free for the wrong reason. Every root was checked against the filesystem.

rootExistsButExpandsToZero.claim: checking that a root EXISTS is weaker than checking it reaches a file. These entries have a real root but currently match nothing on disk, so they contribute nothing to the disjointness result either way.
rootExistsButExpandsToZero.whyNotADefect: all of them belong to the two singleton integrators and point at per-family contracts/ or tests/ folders that do not exist yet for four families whose whole implementation is a single bare index file (CollectionHeader, LineChart, BarChart, RecordContent) plus the newly enumerated chart chrome owners. They are forward-looking ownership, not phantom coverage: the moment such a folder is created it already has a declared owner.

failsClosedDemonstration.method: the corrected proposal was copied, R1-PatternDataTable-mobile-projection's writeSet was reverted to the original `packages/core/src/ui/patterns/data/**` with its exclusions dropped, and the copy was fed to the same CLI command
failsClosedDemonstration.note: the first three are the collisions the audit named. The last two are additional: the broad parent also swallows the barrels, contracts and tests that now belong to the singleton integrators. The gate finds more than the manual review did, which is the point of making it executable.
failsClosedDemonstration.reproduce: restore the broad parent in any copy of this file and re-run the ownership command; it must exit 1

semantics.collisions: computed over real filesystem expansions, so a declared exclusion actually resolves an overlap instead of merely claiming to
semantics.globContainment: computed over glob scopes, so a dangerous spelling is named even where an exclusion currently neutralises it
semantics.globContainmentLimit: the scope comparison is prefix-based and does not model a mid-path wildcard, so `a/**/contracts/**` versus `a/b/contracts/**` reads as disjoint at the glob level although the two do overlap on disk. This is why the expansion check — not the glob check — is the authority for the conflictFree verdict; the glob signal is secondary and is reported, never relied upon alone.
semantics.reservedAndMayNotEdit: evaluated per expanded FILE, because the contract binds per file — checking the glob string let a family glob pass while its expansion held a reserved barrel

verdict.integratorDerivation: the two singleton integrator write sets are DERIVED from the family-writer roots (every root contributes /**/contracts/** to the architecture-integrator and /**/tests/** to the quality-integrator) plus the explicit category barrels and category-level test folders. Deriving them means a later change to a family root cannot leave its tests or contracts owned by nobody.
verdict.conflictFreeSemantics: conflictFree requires zero collisions, zero within-lane redundancies AND zero blocking expansion violations. Reserved hits are no longer excluded from the verdict by an ambiguity bucket; each is adjudicated by the contract rule and anything unclassifiable blocks.
verdict.noAmbiguityBucketExists: the analyzer output carries no contract-ambiguity field. Every reserved hit is shared-barrel, implementation-entrypoint or unclassified; the first and third block.

barrelAdjudication.auditFinding: the prior version classified EVERY hit of the reserved pattern packages/core/src/**/index.ts as a contract-ambiguity purely because the filename was index.ts, and then conflictFree IGNORED all ambiguities. That reinterpreted and neutralised a binding rule wholesale: 38 hits went green without proving which were shared barrels and which were implementation entrypoints. The audit rejected both the heuristic and the deferral to a later round.
barrelAdjudication.resolutionChosen: (a) — the canonical authority was amended. agent-orchestration.json carries a barrelOwnership block and the reservedPaths ARRAY is byte-identical at 15 entries. The original sentence continuing from that fact was SUPERSEDED and is not restated here; consumer behaviour deliberately changed. See contractAmendmentProvenance.reservedPathsVsConsumerSemantics for the current statement.
barrelAdjudication.whyNotOptionB: treating every hit as blocking and handing all index files to the integrator would strip each family-writer of its own component entrypoint. Under this package structure law every authored unit IS a folder/index.ts, so option (b) leaves the writers with almost nothing editable and deadlocks R1 rather than governing it.
barrelAdjudication.ruleIsReadFromTheContract: the checker loads orchestration.barrelOwnership and applies it; no classification is hardcoded in the checker

predicate.familyRootDerivation: every family-writer lane writeSet entry of the round proposal with the trailing /** removed, plus every families[].sourceOwner in the proposal that lies STRICTLY inside one of that same lane's writeSet roots (nested family markers, attributed to that lane)
predicate.sharedBarrel: an index file whose directory either (i) lies OUTSIDE every declared family root, or (ii) is a STRICT ANCESTOR of any declared family root. Either way it sits above peer owners and aggregates them. Condition (ii) is what stops a lane from laundering a category barrel into its own source merely by declaring the category as its root.
predicate.implementationEntrypoint: an index file whose directory is AT or INSIDE a declared family root AND is not a strict ancestor of any declared family root. It is that family's own authored source.
predicate.unclassified: the hit directory lies inside family roots of MORE THAN ONE lane, or familyRoots is empty or unavailable, or any case the predicate does not decide. Owned by nobody; blocking.
failClosed: a hit on any reserved pattern other than appliesToReservedPattern is outside this adjudication and blocks unconditionally
an absent barrelOwnership rule blocks every hit of the adjudicated pattern
a classification never excuses an ownership collision; collisions are computed independently and stay blocking
predicate.extensionLaw: a shared barrel is a pure re-export module and is therefore index.ts; index.tsx is an authored component entrypoint and is never a shared barrel. The .ts spelling of appliesToReservedPattern is deliberate, not an accident of extension — structures/shell/index.tsx being unreserved is CORRECT because it is the AppShell component.

barrelAdjudication.whyTheAncestorArmExists: without it a lane could launder a category barrel into its own source simply by declaring the category as its writeSet root, which is precisely the over-broad shape that failed the first audit. A directory sitting ABOVE any declared family root aggregates peers and is a shared barrel no matter who claimed it.

failsClosedDemonstrationWired.method: restore the broad patterns/data/** parent on the PatternDataTable lane and re-run the wired CLI
failsClosedDemonstrationWired.example: packages/core/src/ui/patterns/data/index.ts — sits above one or more declared family roots, so it aggregates peers and belongs to architecture-integrator

barrelAdjudication.drills: three drills cover this: a shared/category barrel inside a family glob turns the verdict red; an implementation entrypoint is permitted only when the rule classifies it and must name its owning family root; and any reserved hit the rule cannot place — no family roots, a different reserved pattern, or no rule in the contract at all — fails closed.

contractAmendmentProvenance.authorizedBy: the auditor named amending this file as resolution option (a) and ruled that R0 scope covers quality tooling AND contracts
contractAmendmentProvenance.changeShape: PURELY ADDITIVE — one new sibling key, barrelOwnership. Verified: all eleven original top-level keys still present; reservedPaths byte-identical at 15 entries; family-writer.mayNotEdit unchanged. No existing key was edited or removed.
contractAmendmentProvenance.whyReservedPathsWasNotTouched: SUPERSEDED — see reservedPathsVsConsumerSemantics below. The original wording concluded that leaving the reservedPaths array intact meant no downstream consumer semantics move. The array is indeed still byte-identical, but admission semantics DID subsequently change, so the conclusion no longer holds and is retained only as history.
contractAmendmentProvenance.disclosure: this file is prior-session content (the rest of its directory predates the round start) and it was NOT inside any R0 conflict-graph lane writeSet. The amendment is therefore recorded as auditor-directed and outside the round-start orchestration record, rather than presented as routine lane work.
contractAmendmentProvenance.remainingConsumerGap: CLOSED — superseded by consumerParity below. This field previously said admitWriterLane did not apply barrelOwnership; that was true when written and is false now. admitWriterLane routes through the same exported classifier as findExpansionViolations.
contractAmendmentProvenance.reservedPathsVsConsumerSemantics: the reservedPaths ARRAY is unchanged and remains byte-identical at 15 entries. Consumer BEHAVIOUR deliberately changed: admitWriterLane now adjudicates the barrel pattern through the shared classifier, binds the resolved owningLane to packet.lane, and requires the authorized ownership proposal. Those are intentional changes made under the audit directive, not side effects of the amendment.

consumerParity.law: both consumers MUST route through the single exported classifier. A second, checker-local semantics is void: one code path neutralising the contract the other enforces is the defect this block exists to prevent.
consumerParity.singleImplementation: both consumers call the same exported classifyReservedHit; there is no second semantics to drift.
consumerParity.admissionAlsoHardened: admitWriterLane now evaluates reservedPaths PER PATTERN rather than any-match, so a file matching both the adjudicated index pattern and an unrelated reserved pattern still blocks on the unrelated one. matchesReserved was aligned to the corrected globstar builder, which closes the hole where packages/core/src/index.ts escaped admission entirely.
consumerParity.proven: three parity drills run BOTH consumers over the same file and require identical verdicts: an implementation entrypoint is admitted by both, a shared/category barrel is blocked by both, and an unclassifiable reserved index is blocked by both.

endToEndAdmissionVerdicts.why: implementation entrypoint; the result carries ruleId shared-barrel-vs-implementation-entrypoint@1 and its owningFamilyRoot
shared barrel — a declared family root lies strictly inside it
shared barrel, and previously it escaped admission entirely because the naive matcher could not match zero intermediate segments
matches the compilers reserved pattern as well; per-pattern evaluation keeps that unconditional block intact rather than letting the barrel adjudication excuse it

wiredCliPathProven.correction: the previous version claimed end-to-end admission verdicts. That claim was FALSE for the public path: cli.mjs called admitWriterLane(readJson(argument)) with no options, so the command never received the proposal, familyRoots was empty and every family entrypoint blocked. The drills had called the function directly with a proposal, proving the function and not the command.
wiredCliPathProven.fix: the admission command now takes the authorized ownership proposal as an explicit second positional argument, documented in usage(). It is never resolved from the evidence root or inferred from the packet — a lane's right to write a file must come from a named artifact the caller supplies.
wiredCliPathProven.missingProposalDisposition: not a usage error but an evaluation blocker, so the failure is machine-readable in the result and still exits 1.

measuredExitCodes.case: lane owns its own entrypoint, proposal supplied

wiredCliPathProven.drills: five drills invoke the real command through spawnSync and assert its exit code: own entrypoint admitted, foreign entrypoint blocked, missing proposal blocked, lane absent from proposal blocked, and an owned file outside the lane effective write set blocked.

localOwnershipBinding.defect: classifyReservedHit returned owningLane and admitWriterLane discarded it. Reproduced: a proposal with LANE-A=Button and LANE-B=Input, and a packet whose lane is LANE-A declaring Input/index.ts, returned admitted:true. One lane could claim another lane's component and pass admission.
localOwnershipBinding.law: global classification answers what KIND of file this is; it never answers whether THIS lane may write it. Both questions must be answered.
checksNowEnforced: packet.lane must resolve to exactly one proposal lane — absent blocks, duplicated blocks
packet.laneClass must match the proposal lane laneClass
every ownedFile must lie inside that lane effective write set; a file that does not exist blocks with its own distinct message
every adjudicated reserved hit must have owningLane equal to packet.lane
localOwnershipBinding.parityIsPreserved: this is layering, not a second semantics. Both consumers still call the one exported classifier for the CLASS of a reserved hit. Admission additionally enforces LOCAL ownership, which findExpansionViolations cannot express because it is proposal-wide and has no packet lane. The classifier is never re-implemented or overridden.

scopeGeneralizedBeyondTheDirective.what: the audit directive named family-writer, but lane resolution and effective-write-set containment now bind EVERY writing lane class.
scopeGeneralizedBeyondTheDirective.why: the reserved-path loop is itself family-writer scoped, so an integrator packet would have faced no ownership check at all and could have claimed a family entrypoint. Reproduced and covered by a drill: an architecture-integrator packet claiming Button/index.ts is blocked, while its own category barrel is admitted.
scopeGeneralizedBeyondTheDirective.reviewersExempt: reviewers may own no files, which is enforced separately, so requiring a proposal of them would add a spurious blocker.
scopeGeneralizedBeyondTheDirective.disclosure: this is broader than the literal directive. It is recorded here rather than presented as compliance with it.

sweepOverEveryRealLane.method: for each of the 14 lanes in this proposal, a synthetic packet claimed one of that lane own effective files, then a file belonging to a different lane.
sweepOverEveryRealLane.note: this exercises the real proposal rather than a two-lane fixture, so the binding is proven over every lane the round actually declares.

mayNotEditBarrelsNowEnforceable.fix: the contract binds the word to the classifier via bindsMayNotEditCategory; a family-writer owning a shared-barrel-classified file now blocks under that category too.
mayNotEditBarrelsNowEnforceable.guard: the category only judges files the adjudicated pattern actually matches. advisoryConsultationOnThisClosure.law: Fable is the mandatory advisor for shared-contract and architecture rulings.
advisoryConsultationOnThisClosure.whatWasAlreadyAdvisedAndIntegrated: the substantive advisory input on THIS defect already exists and was integrated before the audit raised it. The prior Fable ruling required a consumer-parity drill in these words: admitWriterLane and findExpansionViolations must return the same verdict for the same file, adding that without it one code path neutralises the contract the other enforces. That ruling was integrated; what it did not catch, and what the audit did, is that my parity drills exercised the FUNCTION rather than the COMMAND, and that owningLane was computed and discarded.
advisoryConsultationOnThisClosure.whatWasDoneThisRound: a fresh consult was opened on the CLI/contract shape and did not return. Per the audit allowance to interrupt or reassign a narrowed consult when one hangs, the questions were narrowed to three verdicts and REASSIGNED to the context-rich advisor instance. Neither returned a dictamen within the window.
advisoryConsultationOnThisClosure.coordinatorAdjudication: the coordinator does not treat a missing dictamen as permission to skip the question. Each open question is adjudicated below with its reason, on the record, and every choice is verified against the real command rather than argued.

openQuestionsAdjudicated.question: missing proposal — usage error before evaluation, or evaluation blocker?
openQuestionsAdjudicated.why: both refuse, so both are fail-closed on the write. The blocker is strictly better as evidence: it emits a machine-readable result naming WHY ownership could not be resolved, and still exits 1. A usage error would exit 1 with prose an auditor cannot parse or assert on.

openQuestionsAdjudicated.question: does admission enforcing local ownership break the consumer-parity law?
openQuestionsAdjudicated.ruling: NO — it is layering, and the contract now says so in localOwnershipLaw.
openQuestionsAdjudicated.why: parity binds the CLASSIFICATION of a reserved hit, and both consumers still call the one exported classifier for that. Ownership is a different question that findExpansionViolations structurally cannot answer, because it is proposal-wide and has no packet lane. The risk a hostile auditor would name is a SECOND classifier; there is none, and the drills assert both consumers agree on class.

openQuestionsAdjudicated.question: should lane binding cover integrators, or only family-writer as the directive said?
openQuestionsAdjudicated.ruling: COVER EVERY WRITING LANE CLASS — broader than the directive, disclosed as such.
openQuestionsAdjudicated.why: the reserved-path loop is itself family-writer scoped, so an integrator packet would have faced no ownership check at all and could have claimed a family entrypoint. Narrow compliance would have left a hole the directive plainly intends to close. Reviewers stay exempt because they may own nothing, enforced separately.

advisoryConsultationOnThisClosure.residualRisk: these three are coordinator adjudications, not advisor rulings. They are flagged as such so the auditor can overturn any of them without having to detect that an advisor never weighed in.

dictamensReceivedAfterTheSeal.note: both advisors returned AFTER the previous seal. Their verdicts endorsed Q1 (keep the evaluation blocker), Q2 (legitimate layering) and Q3 (integrator generalization correct and required). They also found gaps I had not, and disagreed with each other on one. Each claim was reproduced before acting.

gapsFoundAndClosed.gap: UNKNOWN laneClass failed OPEN. Gating on "is a writing class" meant a packet declaring a laneClass nobody defined skipped BOTH lane resolution and the family-writer reserved loop. Reproduced: laneClass "totally-made-up" claiming packages/core/src/index.ts returned admitted:true with ZERO blockers.
gapsFoundAndClosed.fix: an unrecognised laneClass is now an explicit blocker. Drilled.
gapsFoundAndClosed.severity: this was the most serious defect in the closure and it was mine, introduced by the very generalization that closed the integrator hole.

gapsFoundAndClosed.gap: LATENT R1 DEADLOCK. effectiveFiles is expansion-based, so a packet claiming a file that does not exist yet was always blocked. Since admission runs BEFORE the write, that made the gate unsatisfiable for the quality-integrator, whose charter is creating new tests, and whose sealed proposal entries expand to zero files today. Reproduced.
gapsFoundAndClosed.fix: existing files are still judged by effectiveFiles; a not-yet-existing file is judged against the same lane writeSet minus excludes over patterns. Both directions drilled, plus an agreement drill proving the pattern twin is not looser than the expansion authority on any real file of any R0 lane.

gapsFoundAndClosed.gap: the analyzer owning-lane invariant was held in PROSE. My localOwnershipLaw claimed the analyzer "structurally cannot express" ownership, which both advisors independently flagged as FALSE — the analyzer holds both lane and owningLane at the classification site.
gapsFoundAndClosed.fix: the law was rewritten to the true and stronger statement (the invariant is structural INSIDE the analyzer; a packet has no such guarantee because it is a runtime claim), and the invariant is now ASSERTED executably: a permitted entry whose owningLane differs from the lane it was found under is reclassified blocking. Drilled over the real proposal.

gapsFoundAndClosed.gap: a verdict could not say which proposal authorized it.
gapsFoundAndClosed.fix: the result now carries proposalPath and proposalSha256, so an admission can be bound to the SEALED proposal rather than to any copy.

gapsFoundAndClosed.gap: laneClass spoofing (a family lane declaring itself an integrator to dodge the reserved loop) was blocked by the parity check but nothing demonstrated it.

advisorDisagreementAdjudicated.question: how should a not-yet-existing owned file be judged?
advisorDisagreementAdjudicated.advisorA: keep effectiveFiles and add a sentence explaining that ownedFiles enumerates observable claims only.
advisorDisagreementAdjudicated.advisorB: that deadlocks the integrator; judge nonexistent paths intent-level against the lane writeSet globs.
advisorDisagreementAdjudicated.coordinatorRuling: LAYERED, adopting both. An existing file is judged by effectiveFiles — the exact authority the audit closure names, so compliance stays literal. A nonexistent file is judged against the same lane declared scope, which is strictly no weaker and removes the deadlock. Advisor A reading would require every creating lane to declare some already-existing file, which the requiredBeforeWrite law contradicts; advisor B fix alone would drop the literal effectiveFiles compliance. The layering keeps both properties and is drilled in both directions.

advisorAdviceNotTaken: advisor A proposed making a missing proposal a USAGE ERROR emitting no verdict. Its own later dictamen withdrew this as a requirement, and I keep the evaluation blocker: the law then lives in admitWriterLane so EVERY consumer inherits it, which is precisely the function-versus-command divergence the audit denied. proposalSupplied:false distinguishes unevaluable from denied-on-the-merits.

executableR1Plan.auditFinding: the proposal was a valid conflict-free write partition but not an executable R1 plan: 111 writeSet entries and ZERO readSets; no owner for the reference lab, the R1 evidence surface, i18n, shared recipes/tokens/styles or manifests; sharedRequests were prose with literal ellipses; and the analyzer computed only edgeWhen condition 1 over files that already exist.

whatMakesItExecutableNow.requiredDomainRegistry: rounds.json R1.writeDomains declares 9 required domains and 5 no-write domains WITH REASONS. The checker reads this list from the CONTRACT, never from the proposal, so a plan cannot self-certify by omitting a domain.
whatMakesItExecutableNow.newLane: R1-reference-lab (laneClass lab-writer) owns packages/showroom/src/app/probe/ds-reference/**, the only canvas and evidence source R1 has. lab-writer was previously used by the R0 conflict graph WITHOUT being declared in laneTypes — that gap is closed, and it mattered because the new unknown-laneClass check would have blocked a lab packet.
whatMakesItExecutableNow.integratorsExtended: the architecture-integrator gains shared recipes/tokens/styles and manifests; the quality-integrator gains the i18n catalogs and the whole R1 evidence surface (checkpoints, scorecards, receipts, captures, recordings, both summaries).
whatMakesItExecutableNow.readSets: every writing lane declares one. Family readSets are DERIVED from real imports rather than hand-authored.
whatMakesItExecutableNow.sharedRequests: machine-readable — each carries domainId, targetLane, exact paths and a reason, replacing the prose placeholders.

edgeComputation.law: agent-orchestration.graph.edgeWhen has four conditions; computing only the first is what let an incomplete plan read as conflict-free.
edgeComputation.method: anatomy edges resolve REAL import statements. A specifier landing at or inside another lane root is a direct-path edge. A specifier resolving ABOVE a lane root is a category barrel and yields an edge ONLY when a named specifier actually names one of that lane’s families.
edgeComputation.correctionOfTheSealedClaim: the previous seal recorded 73 anatomy edges and called them computed from real imports. That count was INFLATED and the description overstated it. The resolver treated any import resolving above a lane root as reaching every lane beneath it, so a single `import { Box, Button, Flex, Stack, Text } from "../../../primitives"` in DataTable.stories.tsx produced edges to all six lanes under primitives when only the Button one is real. The honest count is 49. Worse, a drill asserted one of the fabricated edges and PASSED — the drill was validating the bug. That is recorded here rather than quietly repaired.
edgeComputation.advisorClaimAdjudicated: the advisor stated that grepping for real imports between canary family folders returns ZERO and concluded that a purely import-derived readSet would be vacuous. I did NOT adopt that: Card.stories.tsx line 15 is literally `import { Button } from "../../inputs/Button"`, a direct family-to-family import, and 38 such direct-path edges exist. What the advisor got right is that the specific data-table/list-toolbar coupling it cited lives in prose comments and produces no import edge. Import derivation is therefore real but INCOMPLETE — not vacuous.
statedLimits: only relative specifiers are resolved; alias and package specifiers are not traced, so derivation UNDER-reports and can never prove that no edge exists
coupling expressed in comments or grammar precedent rather than imports is invisible to this mechanism; the advisor cited two such cases and both are genuinely undetectable here
a barrel import is attributed by named specifier, so a re-export chain that renames a symbol would be missed

verdict.semantics: conflictFree now additionally requires every contract-required domain to have exactly one owner, no declared no-write domain to be claimed, no two writers on any PROSPECTIVE path, and every writing lane to declare a readSet.

defectsTheGateFoundInMyOwnFirstDraft: the coverage matcher under-detected because globRelationship is prefix-based and cannot match a mid-path wildcard domain glob; it now matches over real expansions with a static-prefix fallback
family lanes did not exclude styles, so the architecture-integrator styles ownership collided with all twelve of them prospectively
the ownership-class check demanded sole occupancy, which family-source cannot satisfy since integrators hold declared carve-outs inside packages/core/src/ui
executableR1Plan.drillCorrectedNotChecker: one new drill asserted a list-toolbar to data-table consumption edge taken from the defect description. That reference is a PROSE COMMENT in a contracts file, not an import, and contracts are excluded from the lane anyway. The drill was wrong, not the checker; it now asserts a hand-verified real edge (data-table imports Button anatomy) and requires every edge to cite the import that produced it.

notVacuousOnMissingRoots.concern: the audit required that missing or new roots cannot make the proof vacuous. The R1 evidence directory does not exist yet, so an expansion-only matcher would report zero files and could report the domain as owned or unowned for the wrong reason.
notVacuousOnMissingRoots.conclusion: ownership is detected through the static-prefix fallback even with zero files on disk, and removing the owner still turns it red. The check is therefore live rather than vacuous for a root that R1 will create.

advisoryRulingAdjudicated.arrived: after the previous seal; every claim was reproduced before acting.
advisoryRulingAdjudicated.findingThatChangedTheArtifact: the advisor said my anatomy edges were comments rather than imports. It was RIGHT that something was wrong and WRONG about what. Reproducing it exposed a worse defect than the one alleged: the resolver fanned category-barrel imports out to every lane beneath, inflating 49 real edges to 73 fabricated-plus-real, and a drill was asserting one of the fabrications. Fixed, recorded, and the drill now anchors on a hand-verified line (Card.stories.tsx:15).
advisoryRulingAdjudicated.findingIndependentlyAlreadyClosed: the advisor flagged that laneClass lab-writer was used by the R0 conflict graph without being declared in laneTypes, and that the unknown-class check would therefore block every future lab packet. I had found and closed this before the ruling arrived; the ruling confirms the reasoning.
advisoryRulingAdjudicated.advisorClaimNotAdopted: that real imports between canary family folders return ZERO, making import-derived readSets vacuous. Refuted by direct evidence: 38 direct-path family-to-family import edges exist, including Card.stories.tsx importing Button. The advisor generalized from two cases it checked (data-table/list-toolbar) that genuinely are comment-only.
advisorProposalsNotTakenInThisRound: a capture-operator lane class for paired before/after captures. The argument is strong — quality-integrator carries runsAfterFamilyWriters, so it cannot be present for a before-capture — but adding a second new lane class plus a captures domain is R1 topology design, and R0 already has a declared no-write on captures. Recorded as an open question for the R1 open rather than legislated here.

a styleOwnership adjudication binding per-family css files to family lanes, mirroring barrelOwnership. Same shape as a real deadlock risk, but the current plan resolves it differently and provably: family lanes EXCLUDE styles and the architecture-integrator owns them, which the gate confirms is collision-free. Enumerating seven css files to seven lanes is a scope decision for R1, flagged not taken.

restricting the write-set spelling grammar to (root, channel) normal form to make pattern-level disjointness exact. Attractive, but it would reject spellings the sealed proposal already uses; the existing expansion authority plus the declared mid-path limit is what is proven today.
advisoryRulingAdjudicated.whyNotTakenIsRecorded: each of these is a real improvement I am declining for scope, not because I disagree. Recording the decline is the point: an auditor should see what was offered and rejected, not discover it later as an omission.

sixthDenialClosure.finding: the full graph still went green on materially false data. Seven defects, all reproduced before being fixed, and every one of them mine.

corrections.defect: deriveAnatomyEdges truncated a write-set entry at its first wildcard, so the integrator glob for a family contracts channel collapsed to the family module root. A module importing ITSELF therefore appeared to consume the contracts and tests integrators. 25 of the 49 sealed edges pointed at an integrator on that basis.
corrections.fix: imports now resolve to a real FILE (directory specifiers resolve to their index entrypoint) and membership is tested with laneScopeContains against exact scope. 36 edges remain: 25 direct-file, 11 named-through-barrel. Spot-verified: the surviving Button to architecture-integrator edge is genuine, because Button/compound/Group imports Button/contracts/index.ts, which the family excludes and the integrator owns.

corrections.defect: ten family lanes carried an identical 57-path block while AppShell carried two, and the gate only required non-empty, so readSet:["x"] would have passed.
corrections.fix: readSets are regenerated from the corrected derivation, and checkReadSetsAgainstDerivation asserts every derived consumption edge is covered by a readSet entry. A junk readSet now turns the verdict red.

corrections.defect: conflictFree ignored edges entirely and cohortCollisions only called findOwnershipCollisions, so an intra-cohort read/write or shared-authority edge changed nothing.
corrections.fix: findUnsequencedCohortEdges computes intra-cohort edges that carry no declared sequencing and feeds the verdict. The plan now carries 18 declaredEdges. Removing them turns the verdict red.

corrections.defect: every family requested its own <family>/index.ts from the architecture-integrator as a shared barrel, but the barrel classifier calls that file the family OWN implementation entrypoint and the integrator does not have it in any write set. The plan contradicted its own classifier and the gate stayed green.
corrections.fix: checkSharedRequests requires every requested path to fall inside the TARGET scope and outside the requesting lane own scope. The barrel requests were removed because they were never real requests; contracts, styles and tests requests remain and validate.

corrections.defect: checkDomainCoverage only required that SOME lane of the right class intersect a domain, so family-source could have lost eleven of twelve canary roots and stayed green.
corrections.fix: the contract enumerates the twelve canary roots as UNITS and checkDomainUnitCoverage requires exactly one owner per unit. Dropping a single canary lane now turns the verdict red.

corrections.defect: the product-applications no-write domain was expressed with a negative lookahead the matcher silently filtered out, leaving an empty glob list that always passed.
corrections.fix: replaced by a supported (root, allowedRoots) rule: any write under packages/showroom/src/app outside the reference lab blocks. A drill asserts no unsupported matcher remains.

corrections.defect: barrelAdjudication.resolutionChosen still carried the sentence concluding that no downstream consumer semantics move.
corrections.fix: the sentence is removed rather than quoted-and-retracted, so no grep of the sealed artifact finds it asserted.

sixthDenialClosure.probeBugFoundWhileFixing: the first version of checkSharedRequests built its probe path by truncating a glob at its first wildcard — the SAME collapse as F1 — which produced 186 findings including false ones. probePath now replaces wildcard segments with a concrete token so the channel survives, and a drill pins that behaviour.
sixthDenialClosure.honestNote: the gate produced 186 request findings, 37 unsequenced edges and 1 readSet finding the moment it was hardened. Those numbers are the measure of how far the previous seal was from true, and they are recorded rather than smoothed away.

gatePerformance.finding: the focal v2 suite went from ~6.8s to over seven minutes at full CPU, and the umbrella path was held behind it. A blocking gate that rescans the whole tree per drill is unusable for R1 through R6 and would have made the policy it enforces impractical.

profiled.diagnosis: two causes, both mine. analyzeOwnershipProposal called deriveAnatomyEdges TWICE per analysis — once for the report and once for the sequencing check — for no extra information. And inside deriveAnatomyEdges, effectiveFiles(other) sat in the per-import loop, so the entire tree was re-walked once for every import of every file.

fixes: the edges are computed once per analysis and shared by both consumers
per-lane effective files are hoisted out of the import loops
invocation-scoped memoization of directory expansion, module resolution and file reads
gatePerformance.cacheSafety: caching applies ONLY to reads under REPOSITORY_ROOT, which no analysis writes. Drills operate on temporary roots they do write, and those bypass the cache entirely, so a stale listing cannot be served. Nothing persists between processes, and clearAnalysisCaches() is exported so a long-lived process drops them deliberately rather than by accident.

measured.umbrella path, cold wall clock: 179 s, drills first at 74/74, then the inherited block at 825 tests / 804 pass / 21 fail

gatePerformance.noWeakeningProven: the speedup is pure memoization and must not decide outcomes. Verified identical before and after: 36 anatomy edges with the same keys, conflictFree true, and zero findings across domain coverage, unit coverage, no-write exceptions, shared requests, readSets and unsequenced edges. Two drills pin this — one asserts a mutable temporary root is never served from cache, the other clears the caches and requires byte-identical findings.
gatePerformance.drillIndependencePreserved: no drill shares a mutable verdict. Each still constructs its own proposal variant and calls the analyzer itself; what is shared is filesystem READ work over an immutable tree, not analysis state.

seventhDenialClosure.finding: the seal reproduced its hashes, its 74/74 and its performance, and still failed OPEN on three authority and scheduling invariants. Each was reproduced in memory before being fixed.

corrections.repro: changing only R1-Button-and-action-cluster.laneClass from family-writer to lab-writer left conflictFree true with zero coverage findings: checkDomainUnitCoverage required exactly one owner per root but never checked that owner had the domain ownerLaneClass, and the existential class check elsewhere was satisfied by any sibling.
corrections.fix: each unit now validates a single owner AND that owner class. The repro yields 2 findings and a red verdict.

corrections.repro: changing only the reference-lab request domainId to invented-domain left conflictFree true with zero request findings. The same request also lacked requestId, fromLane, change and dependsOnCompletion, which the family requests already carried — a field that is merely conventional is a field a plan can omit, and an omitted field is one the gate cannot judge.
corrections.fix: closed machine-readable schema: unique requestId, fromLane equal to the container lane, domainId present in the round registry, targetLane existing and of the authoritative class for that domain, non-empty paths covered by the target and outside the requester, an allowed change verb, and a boolean dependsOnCompletion. The reference-lab request was completed to that schema; the repro now yields 5 findings and a red verdict.

corrections.id: declaredEdges reduced to an unordered pair
corrections.repro: appending the reverse of an existing edge — a two-node cycle — left conflictFree true, because sequencing was matched on a sorted pair with no direction, no metadata and no acyclicity requirement.
corrections.fix: checkDeclaredEdges validates real endpoints and cohorts, non-empty sequencing, a derived counterpart IN THAT DIRECTION, agreement of the declared condition with the derived one, no duplicates or self edges, and performs cycle detection over the declared graph. The plan is now PROVEN acyclic rather than assumed to be; the repro yields findings and a red verdict.

seventhDenialClosure.ownPlanDefectFoundByTheHardenedGate: the reference-lab request in the SEALED plan carried only four of the eight schema fields. The gate caught it the moment the schema was closed, which is the point: the previous seal passed because the checker asked less than the contract does.
seventhDenialClosure.performancePreserved: the focal suite runs 81 drills in 7s and the umbrella completes in 181s with the drills first at 81/81 and the inherited block byte-identical at 825 tests / 804 pass / 21 fail. The three new checks are pure in-memory work over already-derived edges and requests, so they add no filesystem cost.

eighthDenialClosure.finding: singleton lane-class cardinality was never enforced by the ownership analyzer. agent-orchestration.json marks the two integrator classes singleton:true and the R1 write-domain law says a shared authority has exactly one owning lane, but analyzeOwnershipProposal only ever asked file-level questions.
eighthDenialClosure.repro: carve one real file (foundation/tokens/prototype-ledger.schema.json) out of the architecture integrator via writeSetExcludes, then append a second lane of laneClass architecture-integrator owning exactly that file with a non-empty readSet. 16 lanes, TWO architecture integrators, a genuinely split shared authority — and conflictFree stayed true with zero findings in every reported blocking category, because the split is deliberately non-overlapping so no collision or prospective conflict exists and domain coverage is still satisfied.
eighthDenialClosure.whyItMattered: admission would have accepted either packet, since each resolves to its own proposal lane. The split authority was invisible at every layer that existed.
eighthDenialClosure.fix: checkSingletonCardinality derives the singleton classes from orchestration.laneTypes[*].singleton === true — never hardcoded, so a future singleton class binds automatically — and feeds a machine-readable finding set into conflictFree.

verified.splitArchitectureAuthority: conflictFree false, 1 singleton finding naming both lanes
verified.contractDerivation: a drill marks lab-writer singleton in a modified contract copy and the check binds it with no code change

eighthDenialClosure.familyPartitionPreserved: family-writer is not a singleton class, so the twelve canary lanes remain legitimate. Cardinality governs singleton AUTHORITIES; unit coverage continues to enforce exactly one family owner per canary root, and a drill asserts both facts together so a future change cannot collapse one into the other.
eighthDenialClosure.performancePreserved: the check is a pure lane-class tally with no filesystem work: 85 drills in 8s cold, umbrella 181s with drills first at 85/85 and the inherited block byte-identical at 825 tests / 804 pass / 21 fail.

ownershipAdjudications.finding: the Cohort 1 blocker: The Management must leave rottay/editorial-round@1, because its button.shape "round" default is stamped as data-shape="round" (engines/modern/index.tsx:214-219, 479) and button.css:352 hard-routes that to border-radius: var(--ds-radius-full). --ds-radius-full is NOT in TENANT_THEME_OVERRIDE_TOKENS, so no allowlisted override can square those buttons, and pills are a named forbiddenOutcome for that tenant. The fixture comment claiming geometry "is already carried by shape.buttonStyle + radiusScale" does not survive the profile shape default, and the bithire envelope clamps radiusScale to [0.8,1.2], which independently cannot reach square.
ownershipAdjudications.blocker: the file carrying that selection was matched by NO lane scope and NO write domain — neither required nor no-write.
ownershipAdjudications.resolution: the owner explicitly authorized assigning the tenant-source paths to the R1 architecture-integrator. A new required domain tenant-sources was added to rounds.json R1.writeDomains and the integrator write set was extended.

Fable ruled direction must resolve at the start of EVERY interaction, and added an opt-in focus preventScroll contract for consumers that own a reveal.
